campaignMode.title: Campaign Mode
text: Campaign mode combines all five scenarios in The Rise of Red Skull into one epic experience where the outcome of each game impacts the next scenario. To complete the campaign, the players must win all five scenarios in numerical order, starting with scenario #1 – Crossbones and ending with scenario #5 – Red Skull.
Each player must use their chosen identity for the entire campaign, but they are free to change aspects and alter the contents of their deck following the deck customization rules between scenarios.
When the game ends, if the players won, they follow that scenario’s victory instructions. If the players lost, they may reset the scenario and try again with no penalty.

Cards added to a player’s deck as part of a scenario’s victory instructions must be included in that deck for the rest of the campaign. They do not count toward a player’s minimum or maximum deck size.
Cards 155–162 are campaign-only player cards: they cannot be included in any deck unless the Campaign Instructions direct the players to add them.

newKeywords.title: New Keywords
bullets: Incite X: When a card with the incite X keyword is revealed, place X threat on the main scheme.
Permanent: A card with the permanent keyword cannot leave play.
Piercing: An attack with the piercing keyword discards any tough status cards from the target of the attack before dealing damage.
Ranged: An attack with the ranged keyword ignores the retaliate keyword.
Setup: A card with the setup keyword begins the game in play.

expertCampaign.title: Expert Campaign
text: Each player is numbered 1 to 4 in the campaign log. When a player is instructed to add a card from their expert campaign set to their deck, they take it from the set that matches their player number.

Persistent damage: each player records their remaining hit points after they win a game, which determines their starting hit points for the next scenario (never more than their base hit points). Each scenario’s setup lets a player restore their identity to full hit points by adding an obligation from their expert campaign set to their deck.

A player defeated in a scenario their teammates go on to win does not take part in its victory steps, but can rejoin for the next scenario by adding an obligation to their deck during setup to restore their identity to full hit points.

Obligations in player decks: when a player draws an obligation from their deck, they immediately put it into play in their play area and do not draw a card to replace it. Only the player with the obligation in their play area can use its Alter-Ego Action to deal with it.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Each player searches their deck for all cards with the setup keyword and puts them into play.
Shuffle each Experimental attachment recorded in the campaign log into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Set each player’s hit points to their remaining hit point value recorded in the campaign log for the previous scenario.
Each player may add 1 random obligation from their expert campaign set to their deck to heal their identity to its full hit point value.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Record each identity’s remaining hit points in the campaign log, as well as any cards added to their deck.

intro.title: Scenario #1 – Crossbones
text: Crossbones is attacking the Project P.E.G.A.S.U.S. facility in the Adirondack mountains with a small army of Hydra troops. The S.H.I.E.L.D. soldiers stationed there fight desperately to protect the facility, but they are being overwhelmed by Hydra’s blitzkrieg assault. They need your help to stop Crossbones from capturing the experimental weapons being developed in the P.E.G.A.S.U.S. labs.

rules.title: Experimental Weapons Deck
text: The setup instructions on Attack on Mount Athena 1A instruct the players to create the Experimental Weapons deck: all four cards in the Experimental Weapons encounter set, shuffled together and set facedown next to the main-scheme deck.
After a card from the Experimental Weapons deck enters play, it is considered to be part of the encounter deck. When that card is discarded, it is placed in the encounter deck discard pile.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Each player records their identity in the campaign log. Players cannot switch identities during a campaign.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Each player chooses one of the Tech upgrades from the Hydra Campaign set and adds it to their deck.
Record the name of each Experimental attachment that entered the game in the campaign log.

intro.title: Scenario #2 – Absorbing Man
text: The tide of battle turned against Hydra after you arrived to aid the beleaguered S.H.I.E.L.D. soldiers at Project P.E.G.A.S.U.S. Crossbones has been captured, and his army has been defeated, but Madame Hydra escaped the facility with an Infinity Gem. You chase her outside, but you are stopped short by the imposing form of Absorbing Man. The formidable villain has been hired by Red Skull to delay your pursuit. You will have to defeat him before you can recover the Infinity Gem.

rules.title: Rules Clarification
text: Q. When I put an environment card into play at the beginning of the Absorbing Man scenario, do I trigger the surge keyword?
A. No. The surge keyword only triggers when the card it appears on is revealed. Putting a card into play is not the same as revealing a card.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Record the number of delay counters on the main scheme in the campaign log.
Each player may choose one of the “Basic” Condition upgrades in the Campaign set, attach it to their identity, and add it to their deck in the campaign log.

intro.title: Scenario #3 – Taskmaster
text: With Absorbing Man in S.H.I.E.L.D. custody and Madame Hydra in the wind, you are flying back to Avengers Tower to plan your next move when all reality is changed in a flash of yellow light. When you reach New York City, you are shocked to find Avengers Tower emblazoned with the Hydra banner. But before you can process what has happened, an explosion rocks your Quinjet, and you crash-land in the city.

On the ground, you find that all of New York is under Hydra rule. Anti-hero propaganda is plastered on every corner, and squads of Hydra soldiers patrol the streets. They are led by the notorious Taskmaster, Hydra’s new chief of police. He is going door-to-door hunting down heroes and locking them up. He fired the surface-to-air missile that brought you down, and now he is searching for you.

rules.title: Rules Clarification
text: Q. What happens when I reveal Shadow of the Past and my nemesis minion has the same title as an enemy in play?

A. Your nemesis minion cannot enter the game in this instance, so it will remain set-aside and does not enter the game. However, you still reveal your nemesis’ side scheme and shuffle the rest of your nemesis’s set into the encounter deck. This will cause Shadow of the Past to gain surge as dictated by the card.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Each player who rescued one or more allies from the Taskmaster encounter set adds those allies to their deck and records their names in the campaign log.

intro.title: Scenario #4 – Zola
text: Having defeated Taskmaster, you learn that Hydra has not only captured New York City but all of the United States. It was the mad scientist, Arnim Zola, who built a machine to harness the power of the Reality Gem and tipped the balance of power in Hydra’s favor. He has created a research station for himself on Ellis Island, and turned the historic port into a nightmarish prison for his unfortunate test subjects. Taskmaster was ordered to bring the heroes he captured there for experimentation. In this upside-down America, you are the only hope the captives have to escape a horrible fate.

rules.title: Rules Clarification
text: Q. What does it mean when a card is removed from the campaign log?
A. When a card is removed from the campaign log, cross it out of the campaign log. That card is no longer part of the campaign and cannot be included in any deck for the remainder of the campaign.
Q. If my ally is removed from the campaign at the end of Zola’s scenario, what do I do?

A. If your ally was removed from the campaign, that ally is removed from your deck for the rest of the campaign. If this causes your deck to fall below the minimum number of cards, then you must add a card to your deck.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Each player engaged with an enemy records they are engaged with an enemy in the campaign log.
If the Hydra Prison side scheme is still in play, record the name of each ally underneath it in the campaign log. Those allies cannot be included in any deck for the remainder of the campaign.
If the Hydra Prison side scheme is not in play, each player in hero form may replace their “Basic” Condition upgrade with its “Improved” side.

intro.title: Scenario #5 – Red Skull
text: You have liberated Zola’s island and disarmed the mad doctor, but the Reality Gem still eludes you. You learn from Zola that the Gem resides with the true mastermind behind Hydra’s ascendancy: the brilliant and nefarious Red Skull. The villain has taken up residence in Washington, D.C. and transformed the White House into his personal fortress.

But Red Skull’s ambition for conquest does not end with the U.S.A. — he plans to bind every nation under Hydra rule with the power of the Reality Gem. His scientists work around the clock to make the necessary modifications to Zola’s machine. Once completed, Red Skull will use the Reality Gem to conquer the whole world. If that happens, nobody will be safe from the types of atrocities you witnessed in Zola’s labs. You cannot allow this to happen. You must defeat Red Skull and use the Reality Gem to set things right again.

rules.title: Side Scheme Deck
text: The Setup instructions on The Rise of Red Skull 1A instruct the players to create the side-scheme deck: each side scheme in the encounter deck, shuffled together into their own deck and set next to the main-scheme deck.

The side-scheme deck has its own discard pile. When a side scheme is defeated or otherwise discarded, place it in the side-scheme discard pile. If the side-scheme deck is ever empty, shuffle the side-scheme discard pile into the side-scheme deck. There is no penalty for doing this.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Each player searches their deck for all cards with the setup keyword and puts them into play.
Shuffle each Experimental attachment recorded in the campaign log into the encounter deck.
Place X threat counters on the main scheme, where X is the number of delay counters recorded in the campaign log. (Place X per player instead if you are playing an expert campaign.)

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Each player who was recorded as being engaged with an enemy deals themselves an encounter card.
If the players lose this game, Red Skull conquers the world and the players lose the campaign.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Hydra is defeated and the players win the campaign!

campaignMode.title: Campaign Mode
text: Campaign mode combines all five scenarios in The Galaxy’s Most Wanted expansion into an epic experience where the outcome of each game impacts the next scenario. To complete the campaign, the players must win all five scenarios in numerical order, starting with scenario #1 (Brotherhood of Badoon) and ending with scenario #5 (Ronan the Accuser).
Each player must use their chosen identity for the entire campaign, but they are free to change aspects and alter the contents of their deck following the deck customization rules between scenarios.
When the game ends, if the players won, they follow the Victory instructions at the end of that scenario’s section. If the players lost, they may reset the scenario and try again with no penalty.

Cards #150–177 are the campaign-specific player cards of The Market, and cards #178–187 the campaign-specific encounter cards of the Challenge and Badoon Headhunter sets: they cannot be included in a deck unless players are playing The Galaxy’s Most Wanted campaign.

keywords.title: Important Keywords
bullets: Hinder X: When a card with the hinder X keyword is revealed, place X threat on that card.
Patrol: While any minions with the patrol keyword are engaged with a player, that player cannot thwart the main scheme.
Stalwart: A character that has the stalwart keyword cannot be stunned or confused.

Victory X: When a card with the victory X keyword is defeated, place it in the victory display instead of its owner’s discard pile. The victory display is an out-of-play game area shared by all players.
Amplify icon: When a boost card is turned faceup during an enemy activation, add one additional boost icon to that card for each amplify icon in play.

market.title: Units and The Market
text: Units are the currency used by the Guardians of the Galaxy. While not strictly the reason the Guardians do what they do, it never hurts to turn a profit, and they’re always looking for the opportunity.

Between scenarios, players can spend the units recorded in their campaign log to add cards from The Market to their deck: choose a card whose Unit Cost is no more than your unspent units, subtract its Unit Cost from them, and the card is added to your deck. Repeat as you wish.

Cards added to a player’s deck this way must be included in that player’s deck for the rest of the campaign and do not count toward that player’s minimum or maximum deck size. Only one copy of each card from The Market can be used during a campaign for the players as a group.

expertCampaign.title: Expert Campaign
text: Some Setup and Victory instructions are preceded by Expert Campaign Only. Ignore these instructions unless you are playing an expert campaign.

Persistent damage: each player records their remaining hit points in the campaign log after they win a game (never more than their base hit points). This determines each player’s starting hit points for the next scenario. The Setup instructions of the last four scenarios let players heal their identity to its printed hit point value by subtracting units.

Elimination and victory: a player defeated during a scenario their teammates go on to win does not participate in its Victory steps, but can rejoin their teammates for the next scenario, healing their identity to its printed hit point value.

Deck customization: once a player starts an expert campaign, they cannot add, remove, or change the aspect and/or basic cards in their deck for the remainder of the campaign. Campaign-specific cards can still be added as per the campaign rules.

intro.title: Scenario #1 – Brotherhood of Badoon
text: The Brotherhood of Badoon has mounted a surprise attack against Earth! You and the other Guardians of the Galaxy rush to Earth’s aid, teaming up with the mighty Avengers in the process to beat back the Badoon. However, the Brotherhood of Badoon’s leader, Drang, is a skilled tactician with a fleet of powerful ships and an overwhelming number of soldiers at his side. This won’t be an easy fight.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Each player records their identity in the campaign log. (Players cannot switch identities during a campaign.)
Reveal the Badoon Blitz side scheme (use the reverse side for expert mode).
Shuffle the Badoon Headhunter minion into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: In player order, each player must discard cards from the top of the encounter deck until they discard a minion, then put that minion into play engaged with them.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Record units in each player’s respective “Unspent Units” box (add these to units you already have):
Record 1 unit for each player.
Record a number of units for each player (to a maximum of 3 units) equal to the victory values on encounter cards in the victory display.
Record 1 unit for each player if there are no minions in play.
Record 1 unit for each player if the main scheme is on stage 1B (Terrestrial Invasion).
If Badoon Headhunter is in the victory display, mark the box beside “Scenario #1 – Brotherhood of Badoon” in the “Headhunter Defeated?” section.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Record each identity’s remaining hit points.

intro.title: Scenario #2 – Infiltrate the Museum
text: Though the Badoon were formidable, the teamwork and coordination between the Avengers and Guardians was enough to quell Drang’s onslaught. After the battle, Gamora is able to extract critical information from Drang about why they attacked Earth by using a few... persuasive... interrogation techniques.

As it turns out, Taneleer Tivan—better known as the Collector—heard about the Reality Stone on Earth. Already having the Power Stone in his possession, and always looking to expand his collection, he hired the Badoon to steal Earth’s Stone. Deciding it best if the Collector has no Stones at all, you set out toward his museum.

rules.title: The Collection
text: Throughout the course of the Infiltrate the Museum scenario, cards may be added to “The Collection”. The Collection is an out-of-play game area shared by all players and specific to this scenario. Cards in The Collection follow the standard rules for out-of-play cards.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Reveal the Gallery of Splendor side scheme (use the reverse side for expert mode).

Shuffle the Badoon Headhunter minion into the encounter deck. Then, if there is at least 1 mark in the “Headhunter Defeated?” section of the campaign log, shuffle the On the Hunt treachery into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Set each player's hit points to their remaining hit point value recorded in the campaign log for the previous scenario.
Each player may subtract 1 unit from their respective “Unspent Units” box in the campaign log to heal their identity to its printed hit point value.
In player order, each player must choose 1 card from their hand and put it faceup into The Collection.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Record units in each player’s respective “Unspent Units” box (add these to units you already have):
Record 1 unit for each player.
Record a number of units for each player (to a maximum of 3 units) equal to the victory values on encounter cards in the victory display.
Record 1 unit for each player if there are 1 per player or fewer cards in The Collection.
Record 1 unit for each player if there is no threat on the main scheme.
In the “Cards in The Collection” section, record the title of each player card in The Collection.
If Badoon Headhunter is in the victory display, mark the box beside “Scenario #2 – Infiltrate the Museum” in the “Headhunter Defeated?” section.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Record each identity’s remaining hit points.

intro.title: Scenario #3 – Escape the Museum
text: So... things didn’t go as planned. The good: you broke into the Collector’s museum; you beat the Collector; you know the Power Stone was here. The bad: an alarm went off as soon as you arrived, alerting the Collector to your presence; after you beat the Collector, he used his Elder God magic to trap you in his collection; also, someone else seems to have stolen the Power Stone.

Kind of a mixed bag here. On the bright side, whoever took the Power Stone cut the museum’s power as a distraction, giving you enough time to get out of captivity. Maybe, just maybe, you can leverage this luck and escape the museum before the Collector realizes what’s going on.

rules.title: Infinite Hit Points
text: In this scenario, the villain has infinite hit points (∞). A character with infinite hit points cannot be defeated by taking damage. However, damage may still be dealt to that character through attacks and card abilities.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Reveal the “There Is No Escape” side scheme (use the reverse side for expert mode).

Each player must search their deck, discard pile, and hand for each of their cards recorded in the “Cards in The Collection” section of the campaign log, then remove those cards from the game. Each player draws up to their hand size.

Shuffle the Badoon Headhunter minion into the encounter deck. Then, if the number of marks in the “Headhunter Defeated?” section of the campaign log is equal to or greater than: (1) shuffle the On the Hunt treachery into the encounter deck; (2) shuffle the Dead to Rights treachery into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Set each player's hit points to their remaining hit point value recorded in the campaign log for the previous scenario.
Each player may subtract 1 unit from their respective “Unspent Units” box in the campaign log to heal their identity to its printed hit point value.
In player order, each player must discard cards from the top of the encounter deck until they discard an attachment, then reveal that card.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Record units in each player’s respective “Unspent Units” box (add these to units you already have):
Record 1 unit for each player.
Record a number of units for each player (to a maximum of 3 units) equal to the victory values on encounter cards in the victory display.
For every 2 Galactic Artifacts side schemes in the victory display, record 1 unit for each player.
Record the title of each Galactic Artifacts side scheme in the victory display.
If Badoon Headhunter is in the victory display, mark the box beside “Scenario #3 – Escape the Museum” in the “Headhunter Defeated?” section.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Record each identity’s remaining hit points.

intro.title: Scenario #4 – Nebula
text: As you get out of range of the museum, the Milano’s sensors pick up another speeding ship within your vicinity. Assuming it must be the thief who stole the Stone, you crank up the hyper thrusters and ride the ship’s tail. When you get close, you realize you’re chasing Nebula, daughter of Thanos, and Gamora’s dear sister.
It would be best if she didn’t have the Power Stone, either.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Reveal the Guerrilla Tactics side scheme (use the reverse side for expert mode).

Shuffle each Galactic Artifacts side scheme recorded in the “Galactic Artifacts Side Schemes in the Victory Display” section of the campaign log into the encounter deck. For each: Hujadarian Monarch Egg, place 1 evasion counter on Nebula’s Ship; Magical Teapot, deal the first player 1 facedown encounter card; Philosopher’s Stone, give Nebula 1 facedown boost card; Crystal Ball, give Nebula a tough status card.

Shuffle the Badoon Headhunter minion into the encounter deck. Then, if the number of marks in the “Headhunter Defeated?” section of the campaign log is equal to or greater than: (1) shuffle the On the Hunt treachery into the encounter deck; (2) shuffle the Dead to Rights treachery into the encounter deck; (3) shuffle the Headhunter’s Henchman minion into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Set each player's hit points to their remaining hit point value recorded in the campaign log for the previous scenario.
Each player may subtract 1 unit from their respective “Unspent Units” box in the campaign log to heal their identity to its printed hit point value.
Discard cards from the top of the encounter deck until a Technique attachment is discarded this way, then attach that card to Nebula.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Record units in each player’s respective “Unspent Units” box (add these to units you already have):
Record 1 unit for each player.
Record a number of units for each player (to a maximum of 3 units) equal to the victory values on encounter cards in the victory display.
Record 1 unit for each player if there are 1 or fewer evasion counters on the Nebula’s Ship environment.
Record 1 unit for each player if the main scheme is on stage 1B (The Art of Evasion).
If Badoon Headhunter is in the victory display, mark the box beside “Scenario #4 – Nebula” in the “Headhunter Defeated?” section.
If the Power Stone is attached to an identity, record that identity’s name in the “Power Stone Control” section.
Record the number of evasion counters on Nebula’s Ship in the “Evasion Counters” section.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Record each identity’s remaining hit points.

intro.title: Scenario #5 – Ronan the Accuser
text: Later, aboard the Milano: Nebula set off the alarm on the Collector’s ship — she needed a distraction to reach the Collector’s vault. What to do with the Stone? Groot and Rocket could use the money; Star-Lord won’t just sell it. Cosmo says that if you bring the Stone to him on Knowhere, he can keep it safe.

With a sigh of relief, you kick back in your pilot seat and set course for Knowhere. You have the Power Stone and you’ve captured Nebula. After a discussion with the other Guardians, you decide it best to hand both over to the authorities... because it’s the right thing to do.
The reward money may also be an incentive.

As Knowhere comes into sight, a massive Kree warship suddenly drops out of hyperspace in front of you, intercepting your course. Ronan the Accuser. He sends a brief transmission through your comms relay—something about standing accused? Yeah, that seems appropriate.
Then, he attacks.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: (Optional) Reveal the Kree Supremacy side scheme (use the reverse side for expert mode).

If a player’s identity was recorded in the “Power Stone Control” section of the campaign log, search the encounter deck and discard pile for one copy of the “You Stand Accused!” treachery, then deal that card to that player as a facedown encounter card.

Search the encounter deck and discard pile for one copy of the Pincer Maneuver side scheme and reveal it. Place X per player additional threat on Pincer Maneuver, where X is equal to 3 minus the recorded number in the Evasion Counters section of the campaign log.

Shuffle the Badoon Headhunter minion into the encounter deck. Then, if the number of marks in the “Headhunter Defeated?” section of the campaign log is equal to or greater than: (1) On the Hunt; (2) Dead to Rights; (3) Headhunter’s Henchman; (4) shuffle the Fugitive Recovery side scheme into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Set each player's hit points to their remaining hit point value recorded in the campaign log for the previous scenario.
Each player may subtract 1 unit from their respective “Unspent Units” box in the campaign log to heal their identity to its printed hit point value.
Place an additional 1 per player threat on the main scheme.
If the players lose this game, Ronan the Accuser claims the Power Stone and the players lose the campaign.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Ronan the Accuser is defeated and the players win the campaign!

conclusion.title: Conclusion: Knowhere
text: “We will be keeping the Stone in our most secure vault. It is being kept safe there.” — Cosmo
“Thank you, Cosmo. We have a prisoner as well.”
Gamora: “What were you thinking when you stole the Stone? You know you can’t just sell something like that.” Nebula: “I had to tell my crew something.”
Nebula: “You know what will happen if our father learns where it is.”

campaignMode.title: Campaign Mode
text: Campaign mode combines all five scenarios in The Mad Titan’s Shadow into one epic experience where the outcome of each game impacts the next scenario. To complete the campaign, the players must win all five scenarios in numerical order, starting with scenario #1 (Ebony Maw) and ending with scenario #5 (Loki).
Each player must use their chosen identity for the entire campaign, but they are free to change aspects and alter the contents of their deck following the deck customization rules between scenarios.
When the game ends, if the players won, they follow that scenario’s Victory instructions in order. If the players lost, they may reset the scenario and try again with no penalty.
The campaign log tracks the campaign pool: cards the Victory instructions add to it come into later scenarios as their Setup instructions say.
Cards 180–193 were created specifically for this campaign: they cannot be included in any deck unless the Campaign Instructions direct the players to add them.

expertCampaign.title: Expert Campaign
text: Some Setup and Victory instructions are preceded by Expert Campaign Only. Ignore these instructions unless you are playing an expert campaign.

Persistent damage: each player records their remaining hit points in the campaign log after they win a game (never more than their base hit points). This determines each player’s starting hit points for the next scenario. The Setup instructions offer each player the opportunity to restore their identity to its full hit point value by placing an acceleration token on the main scheme.

A player defeated during a scenario their teammates go on to win does not participate in its Victory steps, but rejoins them for the next scenario by placing an acceleration token on the main scheme to restore their identity to full hit points.
If the players lose the last scenario, Loki, they lose the campaign.

conclusion.title: Conclusion: Asgard
text: Odin: “Throw him in the dungeon and lock the Infinity Gauntlet in the vault. Never again will it trouble the Nine Realms.”
Odin: “Come my friends. There is to be a feast held in your honor!” Thor: “More drinks for my friends — the heroes of Midgard!”
Lady Sif: “That is a fine sword you carry.” “Thank you, m’lady.” “Tell me again how you cut the Infinity Gauntlet from Thanos’ arm.”
Heimdall: “As reward for your service, Odin has ordered the vault of Asgard opened to you. Take what you can carry.” Rocket: “Holy flark balls, Groot! We’re getting paid!”

intro.title: Scenario #1 – Ebony Maw
text: The Mad Titan, Thanos, is on a quest to collect all six Infinity Stones and join them together in the Infinity Gauntlet. If he succeeds, Thanos will have the power to control the universe — or destroy it.

His fanatical followers, the Black Order, have pledged their lives to the Titan’s cause, and they scour the universe for the only two stones that their master still needs to complete the Gauntlet: the Power Stone and the Reality Stone.

One of those followers, Ebony Maw, has discovered that the Power Stone is being kept in a secure vault on Knowhere. Now, the Black Order’s sorcerer is leading an army of Thanos in a direct assault on the space station. Cosmo and the rest of the Knowhere Corps are doing what they can to defend the station, but they won’t last long against Maw without your help!

rules.title: Spell Environment Cards
text: Ebony Maw’s set contains eight Spell environment cards. When a player reveals a Spell environment, they place that card in front of them in their play area, with its invocation counters.

When Ebony Maw activates against a player, an invocation counter is removed from each Spell in their play area, before that activation resolves. A Spell resolves its ability as its last invocation counter is removed.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Each player records their identity in the campaign log. Players cannot switch identities during a campaign.
Put the “Secure the Landing Pad” side scheme into play.
Shuffle the “Security Breach” side scheme into the encounter deck.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: If Secure the Landing Pad was defeated, add Cosmo to the campaign pool.
If Attack on Knowhere 1B was completed, add Security Breach to the campaign pool.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Record each identity’s remaining hit points in the campaign log.

intro.title: Scenario #2 – Tower Defense
text: Ebony Maw failed to capture the Power Stone, but in an unexpected twist, it was delivered to Thanos by Loki, the God of Mischief. The outcast prince of Asgard also revealed to Thanos that the Reality Stone could be found in Avengers Tower on Earth. The Mad Titan immediately ordered Corvus Glaive and Proxima Midnight, his two most trusted generals, to attack the Avengers and seize the last Infinity Stone. Now it’s up to Earth’s mightiest heroes to protect the Stone, and their home, from the Black Order.

rules.title: Two Villains, Two Main Schemes
text: Proxima Midnight and Corvus Glaive are both in play, each with a main scheme of their own: Under Siege and The Armies of Thanos. Both main schemes are active each round; encounter cards that refer to “the main scheme” refer to both, and a player’s card refers to the one its player chooses.

Only the villain whose scheme has Focused Defense attached activates in the villain phase, and Focused Defense moves to the other scheme after each player phase. Neither villain can be defeated while the other has hit points.
Avengers Tower is defended: enough damage on its Stronghold side flips it to its Damaged side, and enough on its Damaged side and the players lose.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Put the “Save the Shawarma Place” side scheme into play.
If Security Breach is in the campaign pool, shuffle it into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Set each player’s hit points to their remaining hit point value recorded in the campaign log for the previous scenario.
Each player may place one acceleration token on one of the main schemes to heal their identity to its full hit point value.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: If Save the Shawarma Place was defeated, add Shawarma to the campaign pool.
If Black Swan is NOT in the victory display, add her to the campaign pool.
If Avengers Tower has the Damaged trait, record that in the campaign log.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Record each identity’s remaining hit points in the campaign log.

intro.title: Scenario #3 – Thanos
text: The Black Order’s assault on Avengers Tower was brutal, but the Avengers stood firm in the defense. The tide of battle turned when the Guardians of the Galaxy arrived to lift the siege. The combined forces of the Guardians and the Avengers was enough to drive back the armies of Thanos. Yet in the midst of that chaos, the Mad Titan used the Space Stone to teleport directly into Avengers Tower. Once inside, he seized the Reality Stone and teleported back to his enormous space ship, Sanctuary.

With all six Infinity Stones in his possession, it is only a matter of time before Thanos masters the power of the Infinity Gauntlet and wreaks havoc on the universe. You only have one shot at stopping him before it’s too late!

rules.title: The Infinity Gauntlet
text: The Infinity Gauntlet is attached to Thanos, and the six Infinity Stones are a deck of their own. After Thanos activates against you, each Infinity Stone in play resolves its Special ability; with none in play, the top Infinity Stone is put into play instead.
While Sanctuary is in play, Thanos cannot take damage from player cards.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Put the “Hack Sanctuary’s Computer” side scheme into play.
If Cosmo is in the campaign pool, put him into play under the first player’s control.
If Security Breach is in the campaign pool, shuffle it into the encounter deck.
If Shawarma is in the campaign pool, each player shuffles one copy of Shawarma into their deck.
If Black Swan is in the campaign pool, put her into play engaged with the first player.
If Avengers Tower had the Damaged trait, deal three damage to each identity (after the Expert Campaign Only instructions).

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Set each player’s hit points to their remaining hit point value recorded in the campaign log for the previous scenario.
Each player may place one acceleration token on the main scheme to heal their identity to its full hit point value.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: If Defensive Protocols is NOT in the victory display, add System Shock to the campaign pool.
If The Infinity Stones 1B was completed, record that in the campaign log.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Record each identity’s remaining hit points in the campaign log.

intro.title: Scenario #4 – Hela
text: Against all odds, Thanos has been defeated and the Infinity Gauntlet wrested from his hand! The combined power of the Guardians of the Galaxy and the Avengers was just enough to save the universe from the Mad Titan.

The heroes all breathe a huge sigh of relief, but they have to decide what to do with the Infinity Gauntlet. Tensions rise among the super-powered friends as an impassioned debate breaks out. Before the argument can spiral further out of control, the enigmatic Adam Warlock steps forward to offer his stewardship. His unique connection to the Soul Stone makes him the ideal candidate to safeguard the Gauntlet. The gathered Avengers and Guardians agree to this, and the Gauntlet is entrusted to Warlock’s care.

Relieved to have the matter settled, the exhausted heroes move to the lounge to eat and celebrate their victory. After they leave, the stoic figure of Adam Warlock is replaced by the grinning God of Mischief. Loki used his magic arts to impersonate Warlock and fool the heroes into giving him the Infinity Gauntlet! The trickster uses the power of the Gauntlet to enact the final part of his plan: to usurp the Throne of Asgard from Odin. He casts the All-Father down to Hel, consigning him to the cruel ministrations of Hela, goddess of death. Only the stalwart watchman of Asgard, Heimdall, escapes to bring news of Loki’s treachery to Avengers Tower. He warns that only Odin has the power to defeat Loki and insists that the heroes journey into Hel to rescue the All-Father from Hela’s grasp.

rules.title: Infinite Hit Points, Journey Through Hel
text: Hela’s Wounded side has infinite hit points: she cannot be defeated by taking damage. After a side scheme is defeated, she flips to her Mystic side.

Odin is attached to the main scheme, Odin’s Torment, on his Captive side. While he is, Hela would be defeated, she flips to her Wounded side instead. Defeat the side schemes on the road through Hel to free Odin: once the first player controls him, Hela can be defeated. If Odin (Captive) leaves play, the players lose.

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Put the “Find the Norn Stones” side scheme into play.
Shuffle the “Summoned Back” treachery into the encounter deck.
If Shawarma is in the campaign pool, each player shuffles one copy of Shawarma into their deck.
If System Shock is in the campaign pool, each player shuffles one copy of System Shock into their deck.
If The Infinity Stones 1B was completed, each player discards the top half of their deck.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Set each player’s hit points to their remaining hit point value recorded in the campaign log for the previous scenario.
Each player may place one acceleration token on the main scheme to heal their identity to its full hit point value.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: If Find the Norn Stones was defeated, add Norn Stone to the campaign pool.
If Retrieve Odin’s Armor is in the victory display, add Odin to the campaign pool.

expertVictory.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Record each identity’s remaining hit points in the campaign log.

intro.title: Scenario #5 – Loki
text: The heroes have defeated Hela and rescued Odin from the dungeons of Hel, but Loki still sits on the throne of Asgard with the Infinity Gauntlet. Heimdall can take you to the Golden Realm, and the All-Father can offer you some protection from Loki’s magic, but it is up to you to defeat the trickster god and secure the Infinity Stones.

rules.title: Winning the Game
text: Five versions of Loki make the villain deck: one in play at random, the others set aside. When Loki is defeated he goes to the victory display and a random set-aside Loki takes his place, with all that was on him.
The first player chooses the victory condition as the game begins: the number of Lokis in the victory display that wins the game (1 rookie, 2 standard, 3 expert, 4 heroic).

setup.title: Campaign Instructions: Setup
bullets: Put the “Open the Dungeons” side scheme into play.
Shuffle the “Summoned Back” treachery into the encounter deck.
If Shawarma is in the campaign pool, each player shuffles one copy of Shawarma into their deck.
If System Shock is in the campaign pool, each player shuffles one copy of System Shock into their deck.
If The Infinity Stones 1B was completed, each player discards the top half of their deck.
If Norn Stone is in the campaign pool, each player puts one copy of the Norn Stone upgrade into play on its Setup side.
If Odin is in the campaign pool, put Odin into play on his King side.

expertSetup.title: Expert Campaign Only
bullets: Set each player’s hit points to their remaining hit point value recorded in the campaign log for the previous scenario.
Each player may place one acceleration token on the main scheme to heal their identity to its full hit point value.
If the players lose this game, Loki exerts his rule over all the universe and the players lose the campaign.

victory.title: Campaign Instructions: Victory
bullets: Loki is defeated and the players win the campaign!

campaignMode.title: Sinister Motives: Campaign Mode
text: Win the five scenarios in order: Sandman, Venom, Mysterio, the Sinister Six, then Venom Goblin. Keep the same identity throughout the campaign; aspects and deck contents may change between scenarios. A loss may be retried without penalty, except Venom Goblin in an expert campaign.

Reputation is shared by the group. At each victory, gain the victory points in the victory display plus 1 for each condition met: no minions, no side schemes, no threat on the main scheme, fewer acceleration tokens than players, and no defeated identities.

White reputation effects resolve when their node is first marked. Pink setup effects apply to later scenarios, left side from top to bottom, then right side from top to bottom. Tech and Aspect Advantage cards added by reputation do not count toward deck size.

Venom (Eddie Brock) and Symbiote Suit cannot be included in campaign decks unless a campaign rule allows them. Osborn Tech and Sinister Assault modular sets are included only when campaign instructions direct it.

expertCampaign.title: Expert Campaign
text: After a victory, record remaining hit points up to the identity’s printed hit points. The next scenario starts at the recorded value. Each scenario offers healing to printed hit points in exchange for facedown encounter cards.
A defeated player does not participate in victory instructions. They can rejoin the next scenario by accepting its healing penalty.
Optionally, lock aspect and basic cards after the campaign begins. Campaign rewards may still be added as instructed.

intro.title: Sandman
text: Sandman fills the streets with tidal sands as civilians struggle to escape. Stop him before the surrounding city is overwhelmed.

rules.title: Sandman: City Streets
text: Sandman’s first two stages deal indirect attack damage. If his attack damages your identity, resolve Surging Sands: add a sand counter to City Streets, then discard encounter cards equal to its sand counters. His final stage uses overkill instead of indirect damage.

Once per round per player, a hero may exhaust a controlled character to remove sand counters equal to that character’s ATK. Each acceleration token placed on Hapless Pedestrians deals 3 indirect damage to the first player.

setup.title: Campaign Setup: Sandman
bullets: Put Public Outcry into play on the face matching the scenario difficulty.
Shuffle Smear Campaign and one random Community Service side scheme into the encounter deck.

expertSetup.title: Expert Setup: Sandman
bullets: Place 2 additional sand counters on City Streets. Resolve Surging Sands.

victory.title: Campaign Victory: Sandman
bullets: Calculate and gain reputation. Resolve any newly reached immediate reputation effects.
Record a Community Service side scheme in the victory display. In an expert campaign, record each surviving identity’s remaining hit points.

intro.title: Venom
text: Venom charges relentlessly. A nearby bell tower offers a chance to turn its sonic vibrations against him.

rules.title: Venom: Boost Cards and Bell Tower
text: Attacks by your identity or an ally you control that damage Venom place facedown boost cards on your identity. When Venom activates against you, move those cards to Venom for that activation.

While Bell Tower is Quiet, attack damage to Venom may be converted into chime counters. At 3 counters per player, it flips to Ringing. Ringing increases damage Venom takes by 1 and spends chime counters to prevent damage his attacks would deal to identities; at no counters, it returns to Quiet. Converted damage is not excess damage.

setup.title: Campaign Setup: Venom
bullets: Put Public Outcry into play. Shuffle Smear Campaign and a random Community Service side scheme not already completed into the encounter deck.
Resolve marked reputation setup effects: left side top to bottom, then right side top to bottom.

expertSetup.title: Expert Setup: Venom
bullets: Restore recorded hit points. Each player may deal themself 1 facedown encounter card to heal to printed hit points.
Place 1 facedown boost card on each identity.

victory.title: Campaign Victory: Venom
bullets: Calculate and gain reputation; resolve newly reached immediate effects.
Record Community Service in the victory display and, in an expert campaign, remaining identity hit points.

intro.title: Mysterio
text: Inside Oscorp, mirrors and phantoms distort reality. Fight through Mysterio’s illusions before his nightmare consumes you.

rules.title: Mysterio: Encounter Cards in Your Deck
text: Encounter cards may enter your deck or discard pile. When you would draw or discard an encounter card from your deck, deal it to yourself as a facedown encounter card and draw a replacement card. For simultaneous draws, finish drawing the batch before dealing its encounter cards.

Mysterio places resolved Illusion boost cards in your discard pile, on the bottom of your deck, or on the top of your deck according to his stage. Remove all encounter cards from player decks, hands, and discard piles after the scenario.

setup.title: Campaign Setup: Mysterio
bullets: Put Venom (Eddie Brock) into play under the first player’s control. Put Public Outcry into play.
Shuffle Smear Campaign, Snitches Get Stitches, and a random uncompleted Community Service side scheme into the encounter deck.
Resolve marked reputation setup effects, left side then right side.

expertSetup.title: Expert Setup: Mysterio
bullets: Restore recorded hit points. Each player may deal themself 2 facedown encounter cards to heal to printed hit points.
In player order, each player shuffles the top 2 encounter-deck cards into their deck.

victory.title: Campaign Victory: Mysterio
bullets: Calculate and gain reputation; resolve newly reached immediate effects. Record Community Service in the victory display.
Count Illusion cards still in all player decks and record the total as Waking Nightmare. In an expert campaign, record remaining identity hit points.

intro.title: The Sinister Six
text: Mysterio’s illusion gives way to an underground silo. Six villains emerge from the darkness as you search for a way out.

rules.title: The Sinister Six: Escape
text: Only the villain with the active counter activates during the villain phase. Unqualified encounter references to “the villain” mean that villain. Move the counter to the next ascending activation order, wrapping to the lowest as needed.

A villain defeated is set aside and removes 4 threat from a side scheme, or 7 if no other villain remains. Defeating every villain does not win: remove the threat from both sides of Light at the End to escape. If a villain must activate with none in play, Ambush brings one back.

An attack prevented by stun or an attack that deals no damage does not trigger the villains’ damage-dependent counter movement. If villains are in play but none has the active counter when activation is needed, give it to the lowest activation order and continue.

setup.title: Campaign Setup: The Sinister Six
bullets: Put Venom (Eddie Brock) into play under the first player’s control and put Public Outcry into play.
Shuffle Smear Campaign, Snitches Get Stitches, and a random uncompleted Community Service side scheme into the encounter deck.
Place additional threat on Light at the End equal to Waking Nightmare. Resolve reputation setup effects, left side then right side.

expertSetup.title: Expert Setup: The Sinister Six
bullets: Restore recorded hit points. Each player may deal themself 2 facedown encounter cards to heal to printed hit points.

victory.title: Campaign Victory: The Sinister Six
bullets: Calculate and gain reputation; resolve newly reached immediate effects. Record Community Service in the victory display.
Record each villain still in play as Last Ones Standing. In an expert campaign, record remaining identity hit points.

intro.title: Venom Goblin
text: Norman Osborn has bound himself to the symbiote. Stop Venom Goblin’s assault before New York falls under his control.

rules.title: Venom Goblin: The Glider Counter
text: Three main schemes begin in play. Enemy scheming, unqualified encounter effects, and acceleration token placement affect the scheme with the glider counter. Player cards may affect any main scheme.

Each main scheme accumulates its own acceleration threat and tokens. A completed scheme flips to its Symbiote environment and is revealed; move the glider counter and its acceleration tokens to the least-threat main scheme. Two Symbiote environments lose the game. The first player resolves ties for least or most threat.
Patrol and crisis restrict only the scheme with the glider counter. Venom Goblin moves the counter after activating and resolves the destination scheme’s effects according to his stage.

setup.title: Campaign Setup: Venom Goblin
bullets: Put Public Outcry into play and shuffle Smear Campaign into the encounter deck.
Shuffle in the Sinister Assault minion matching each villain recorded as Last Ones Standing.
Resolve reputation setup effects, left side then right side.

expertSetup.title: Expert Setup: Venom Goblin
bullets: Restore recorded hit points. Each player may deal themself 3 facedown encounter cards to heal to printed hit points.
Place 1 additional threat per player on each main scheme. If you lose this game, the campaign is lost.

victory.title: Campaign Victory: Venom Goblin
text: You win the campaign! Optionally calculate one final reputation gain and record the total as your Final Reputation Score.

conclusion.title: New York Is Safe
text: Venom Goblin is defeated. Your final reputation records the objectives achieved throughout the campaign.
